chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The curse, when it goes out from the mouth of its owner, hesitates. So if it finds a way out (to the deserving), or else it returns upon its owner.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a curse if it does not find a deserving recipient?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the metaphysical mechanics of the curse (la'ah), describing it as a spiritual entity that hovers until it finds a 'masagh' (a suitable channel or recipient). In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted to mean that if the curse does not land on the intended target or a worthy substitute, it returns to the utterer, potentially doubling its effect, a concept linked to the principle of 'return of the curse' (ruju' al-la'nah).
